SMTO-SKL-0180 — SMTO isn't sure if your file was added to the release

GUID: e96568b5-763a-5ea1-9dd6-c967b749095f
Slug: github-asset-upload-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO sent a file to a GitHub release, but didn't get a clear answer back. The release may already have the file, or only part of it, so uploading again could fail or create a duplicate.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open Releases, find this release, and open its Assets list. Look for a file with the same name. GitHub may have saved the file even though SMTO didn't get the confirmation.
  2. If a file with that name is there, compare its size with your file. Don't upload it again. GitHub won't accept two files with the same name, and a matching name doesn't prove the file is complete.
  3. If that file looks wrong or incomplete, ask the person who manages releases whether to remove it. Only after it's removed, or if none is there, ask the Agent to upload once. Removing a release file is permanent, so a person should decide rather than SMTO doing it automatically.

What success looks like

  • The release's Assets list shows your file once, with the expected size.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages releases for this project. Don't delete release files without checking with them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The release asset upload lost a reliable response (transport failure, server error, or a reply whose name, size or id did not match), so the asset may be fully, partially, or not uploaded.

What this means

  • Release asset upload loses a reliable mutation result and is classified with its upload-specific unknown outcome. The write may have applied despite its missing or invalid acknowledgement. Read exact provider state and reconcile it before another mutation; matching text alone does not prove attribution.

Why this can happen

  • Release asset upload loses a reliable mutation result and is classified with its upload-specific unknown outcome.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact release assets using provider IDs, name, size and digest where available.

How to fix it

  • Do not upload again. List the release's assets (github.release_assets) and compare asset ID, name, size and digest with the source file's recorded SHA-256; name and size alone do not prove this upload succeeded. Leave any partial or 'starter' asset in place for a deliberate operator decision (github.release_asset_delete) rather than replacing it automatically.
  • Do not upload again. Inspect exact release assets by provider ID, name, size and digest when available; name/size alone do not prove this invocation succeeded. Preserve any starter asset for explicit operator repair.

Retry and execution caution

What not to do
